full_judgment: 16. In Pandit Chunchun Jhn vs Sheikh Ebadat Ali, (1955) 1 SCR 174, Bose, J observed ''the legislation has made a clear cut classification and excluded transaction embodied in more than one document from the category of mortgages, therefore, it is reasonable to suppose that persons who, after the amendment, choose not to use two documents, do not intend the transaction to be a sale, unless they displace that presumption by clear and express words; and if the conditions of section 58(c) are fulfilled, then we are of opinion that the deed should be construed as a mortgage.'' This follows that where the transaction is embodied in one document and once its terms are covered by section 58(c), then there is a presumption that the transaction is a mortgage unless there are express words to indicate the contrary or in case of ambiguity, the attendant circumstances necessarily lead to the opposite conclusion.
